market_context: United States; home refrigeration of fresh and soft cheese
title: How long does fresh cheese last in the fridge?

seo.title: How long does fresh cheese last in the fridge?
seo.meta_description: Fresh cheese is more perishable than aged cheese. Learn how long it lasts refrigerated, what changes after opening and when to discard it.
seo.search_intent: Find out how many days fresh cheese lasts in the refrigerator, especially after opening, and when it should be thrown away.

excerpt: Fresh cheese should stay refrigerated and the package's use-by and after-opening directions should come first. As a broad reference, USDA gives about 1 week in the refrigerator for several soft cheeses at 40 °F or below, but individual fresh cheeses may carry a shorter after-opening instruction.
content_html:
Fresh cheese behaves very differently from a block of aged cheddar or Parmesan. It contains more moisture, has not undergone long aging and is normally eaten ready-to-eat, so its refrigerated window after opening is comparatively short.

The package gives the most specific limit

Two dates or instructions can matter. A printed use-by date applies when the product has been stored as directed, while wording such as “use within 3 days of opening” starts a new, shorter clock once the seal is broken.

Opening introduces oxygen and more opportunities for contamination. A tub opened on Monday should not automatically be treated as good for another ten days simply because the unopened package date is still far away.

What is a reasonable general reference?

USDA lists about 1 week refrigerated for several soft cheeses, including cottage cheese, ricotta and Brie, at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or below. That is a broad home-storage reference, not a reason to ignore a manufacturer's shorter after-opening instruction.

Fresh mozzarella, queso fresco, ricotta, cottage cheese and other high-moisture cheeses are not identical products. Their packaging, salt, acidity and manufacturing process differ, which is why a product-specific label can be more useful than one universal number.

Why fresh cheese is more perishable

High moisture and limited aging mean fresh cheese has fewer hurdles to microbial growth than a dry aged cheese. It is also usually eaten without another kill step such as thorough cooking.

Refrigeration slows many microorganisms but does not sterilize food. Listeria monocytogenes is especially important because it can grow at refrigerator temperatures, and soft cheeses are among the ready-to-eat foods that require careful temperature control.

How to store an opened container

Keep the refrigerator at 40 °F or below, use clean utensils and close the container promptly after serving. If the cheese is packed in brine or liquid, follow the manufacturer's direction about keeping it submerged or retaining the packing liquid.

Avoid repeatedly leaving the whole container on the table through a long meal and putting it back afterward. Time outside refrigeration accumulates; cooling the cheese again does not reverse microbial growth that may already have occurred.

Smell and appearance cannot extend the clock

A distinctly abnormal sour odor, slimy surface, strong color change, unusual liquid, swollen package or unwanted mold are reasons to discard the cheese early. Mold on a soft or fresh cheese is not something to trim away because contamination can extend below the visible area.

The opposite is also important: a normal smell and appearance do not prove that an old fresh cheese is microbiologically safe. Some pathogens produce no obvious sensory warning.

The practical rule

For fresh cheese, keep it cold, follow the label and think in days after opening. USDA's one-week reference for several soft cheeses is useful context, but a package that says “use within 3 days” is the more specific instruction.

faq.question: How long does opened fresh cheese last?
faq.answer: It depends on the product. USDA gives about one week for several soft cheeses, but a package may specify a shorter 2–4 day after-opening period that should take priority.

faq.question: Can I eat fresh cheese after its use-by date?
faq.answer: It is safer not to extend a use-by date on a highly perishable refrigerated cheese. Follow the package date and storage directions.

faq.question: Can I cut mold off fresh cheese and eat the rest?
faq.answer: No. Mold on soft or fresh cheese can extend below the visible surface, so the whole product should be discarded.

faq.question: What temperature should the refrigerator be?
faq.answer: Keep it at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or below for perishable foods such as fresh cheese.
